message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| # | Title | Year | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|---|-------|------|------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | A masterclass in psychological dread, with iconic imagery and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | A brutal, atmospheric descent into grief‑driven terror that redefines the genre. |
| 3 | **Get Out** | 2017 | A smart, socially conscious horror that blends satire with genuine scares. |
| 4 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | A haunting psychological thriller that explores grief and motherhood. |
| 5 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Suspense built on silence, with a tense, emotional core. |
| 6 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | A daylight horror that turns the idyllic Swedish festival into a nightmare. |
| 7 | **It Follows** | 2014 | A fresh take on the supernatural with a relentless, creeping threat. |
| 8 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | A well‑crafted paranormal investigation that balances scares with character depth. |
| 9 | **The Ring** | 2002 | A modern retelling of a Japanese classic, perfect for a quick, chilling binge. |
|10 | **Paranormal Activity** | 2007 | Low‑budget, high‑impact found‑footage horror that still feels fresh. |
|11 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | A meta‑commentary that subverts horror tropes while delivering solid scares. |
|12 | **Suspiria** (2018) | 2018 | A visually stunning, unsettling remake of the 1977 classic. |
|13 | **The Witch** | 2015 | A slow‑burn, atmospheric horror rooted in 17th‑century New England folklore. |
|14 | **It** | 2017 | A nostalgic, terrifying adaptation of Stephen King’s novel, great for a family‑friendly scare. |
|15 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | The quintessential exorcism film that set the standard for supernatural horror. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want psychological dread, supernatural chills, or a blend of both!
